mcqs.question: Centripetal acceleration is best described as:

options.A: An acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path.
options.B: An acceleration tangent to the circular path.
options.C: An acceleration caused by a change in the magnitude of speed.
options.D: An acceleration opposite to the instantaneous velocity.

mcqs.answer: An acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path.
mcqs.explanation: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously. This change in direction requires an acceleration toward the centre of the circle, called centripetal acceleration. Option B describes tangential acceleration, C describes linear acceleration due to speed change, and D is incorrect.

mcqs.question: A car moves at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹ around a circular track of radius 50 m. What is its angular speed in rad s⁻¹?
mcqs.explanation: Angular speed ω = v / r. Substituting v = 20 m s⁻¹ and r = 50 m gives ω = 20/50 = 0.4 rad s⁻¹. The other options result from incorrect division or multiplication.

mcqs.question: A stone tied to a string rotates in a horizontal circle of radius 0.5 m with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of its centripetal acceleration?
mcqs.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a_c = v² / r. Here v = 10 m s⁻¹, r = 0.5 m, so a_c = (10)² / 0.5 = 100 / 0.5 = 200 m s⁻². Options A, C, and D are results of using wrong values or forgetting to divide by r.

mcqs.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit at constant speed. Which statement correctly defines this motion?

options.A: Motion with constant speed and constant direction.
options.B: Motion with constant speed but continuously changing direction.
options.C: Motion with varying speed but constant direction.
options.D: Motion with varying speed and direction.

mcqs.answer: Motion with constant speed but continuously changing direction.
mcqs.explanation: Uniform circular motion means the magnitude of the velocity (speed) stays constant, while its direction changes at every instant as the object follows a circular path. Hence option B is correct. Option A ignores the change in direction, C and D describe non‑uniform motion.

mcqs.question: A particle starts from the positive x‑axis and moves counter‑clockwise to an angle of 60°. Which statement is correct about its angular position?

options.A: It is 60° measured from the positive x‑axis.
options.B: It is the same as the angular displacement of 60°.
options.C: It is always zero for circular motion.
options.D: It equals the linear distance travelled along the arc.

mcqs.answer: It is 60° measured from the positive x‑axis.
mcqs.explanation: Angular position is the angle measured from a reference direction (usually the positive x‑axis) to the radius vector of the particle. Here the particle is at 60° from the reference, so option A is correct. Option B confuses position with displacement; while they are numerically equal in this single‑move case, the definition of position is the angle itself. Options C and D are incorrect definitions.

mcqs.question: Why does an object moving in a circle at constant speed experience a centripetal acceleration toward the centre?

options.A: Because its speed is continuously increasing.
options.B: Because the direction of its velocity changes continuously.
options.C: Because a force acts outward on the object.
options.D: Because gravity is the only force acting.

mcqs.answer: Because the direction of its velocity changes continuously.
mcqs.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. In uniform circular motion the speed (magnitude) is constant, but the direction of the velocity vector changes at every instant, requiring an acceleration directed toward the centre (centripetal). Option A is false (speed is constant). Option C describes a centrifugal effect, which is not a real force. Option D is irrelevant unless the motion is vertical.

mcqs.question: Two particles A and B rotate about the same axis with the same angular speed ω. Particle A is at a radius of 0.2 m, particle B at 0.5 m. Which statement is true?

options.A: Both particles have the same linear speed.
options.B: Particle A has a greater linear speed than particle B.
options.C: Particle B has a greater linear speed than particle A.
options.D: Linear speed is independent of the radius.

mcqs.answer: Particle B has a greater linear speed than particle A.
mcqs.explanation: Linear speed v = ω r. With the same ω, the particle at the larger radius (B) has a larger v. Therefore option C is correct. Options A and D ignore the r dependence, and B reverses the relationship.

mcqs.question: A car travels around a circular track of radius 30 m in 20 s per revolution. What is its centripetal acceleration?
mcqs.explanation: Period T = 20 s, so angular speed ω = 2π/T = 2π/20 = π/10 ≈ 0.314 rad s⁻¹. Linear speed v = ωr = 0.314 × 30 ≈ 9.42 m s⁻¹. Centripetal acceleration a_c = v²/r = (9.42)² / 30 ≈ 88.8 / 30 ≈ 2.96 m s⁻², which rounds to 3.0 m s⁻². Hence option B is correct. The other options result from incorrect arithmetic or omitting a step.
